title: Before I Jump Into Something Else
scene: A new request arrives while you are already working on something important. You acknowledge the message, protect your current focus, leave room for a genuinely urgent exception, and give a realistic time for when you can start the new task.
sceneJa: 大事な仕事を進めている途中で別件が届いた場面。新しい依頼を無視せず受け取ったことを伝えつつ、今の集中を守り、本当に緊急なら優先順位を調整し、そうでなければ現実的な着手時刻を示す。

chunks.en: and I'll take a proper look at it
chunks.ja: そして、きちんと確認します
今取り組んでいるものを

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I don't want to switch tasks / halfway through / unless there's a good reason to.
I don't want / to switch tasks halfway / through unless there's / a good reason to.
I don't / want to switch / tasks halfway through unless / there's a good reason to.
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the main action, the timing phrase, and the exception condition as clear thought units.

questions.question: What does ‘get to it’ mean here?
questions.explanation: In this work context, ‘get to it’ means to reach the task in your workload and start dealing with it.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say ‘If it's more urgent than it looks’?
options: To guarantee the new request will always be delayed
To avoid assuming urgency while still allowing priorities to change if necessary
To stop the current task immediately
questions.explanation: The speaker protects current focus but leaves room to reprioritise if the request is genuinely more urgent than it first appears.

speak: Sound focused rather than annoyed. Say ‘I've seen your message’ lightly to acknowledge the request, give ‘what I'm working on now’ a little emphasis, and keep ‘If it's more urgent than it looks, let me know’ open and flexible. Finish ‘later this afternoon’ clearly so the timing sounds realistic and dependable.
review: Previous session: assumption → reality check → reprioritise → relief. ‘Need immediate attention’ helped separate truly urgent work from tasks that could wait. Today applies the same idea to interruptions: acknowledge → protect focus → allow an exception → give a timeline. Useful chunks are ‘take a proper look at it,’ ‘unless there's a good reason to,’ and ‘adjust my priorities.’
